    Computing different metrics of response's consistency.

    response_consistency.Rd

    Computing different metrics of response's consistency from both double-pass and non double-pass reverse correlation data.

    response_consistency(
  data,
  participant_id = "participant",
  block_id = "block",
  trial_id = "trial",
  feature_id = "feature",
  value_id = "value",
  response_id = "response",
  method = c("calibrated_template", "calibrated_kernel", "full_glm", "intercept",
    "template_distance", "kernel_similarity"),
  double_pass = TRUE,
  link_function = c("logit", "probit"),
  return_by = c("all", "block")
)

    Arguments

    data

    Dataframe, with reverse correlation data (in long format).

    participant_id

    Numeric/Character/Factor, column in data specifying the participant ID.

    block_id

    Numeric, column in data specifying the block ID.

    trial_id

    Numeric, column in data specifying the trial ID.

    feature_id

    Numeric/Factor, column in data specifying the feature.

    value_id

    Numeric, column in data specifying the feature value

    response_id

    Numeric, column in data specifying the response (should be in the 0/1 format).

    method

    Character, which consistency method to use. Options are "template_distance", "kernel_similarity", "intercept", "calibrated_kernel", "calibrated_template", and "full_glm". The calibrated methods estimate trial-wise response probabilities and convert them into expected double-pass agreement.

    double_pass

    Logical, indicating whether the last block was repeated.

    link_function

    Character, which binomial GLM link function to use in the "intercept" method (see ?binomial).

    return_by

    Character. Should metrics be returned per participant and block ("block") or pooled across all eligible blocks per participant ("all")? Defaults to "all".

    Value

    Dataframe, various metrics of response consistency.

    Author

    Ladislas Nalborczyk ladislas.nalborczyk@cnrs.fr.

    Examples

    if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# import the self-voice data
data(self_voice)
head(self_voice)

# compute response consistency per participant
response_consistency(self_voice, method = "template_distance") |> head(10)
response_consistency(self_voice, method = "kernel_similarity") |> head(10)
response_consistency(self_voice, method = "intercept") |> head(10)
response_consistency(self_voice, method = "intercept", link_function = "probit") |> head(10)
response_consistency(self_voice, method = "calibrated_kernel")
response_consistency(self_voice, method = "calibrated_template")
response_consistency(self_voice, method = "full_glm")

# compute response consistency per participant and block
response_consistency(self_voice, method = "full_glm", return_by = "block")
} # }
